rulings.rationale: The amendment identifies a real pattern weakness in 2 of 3 migration tests, but the existing test suite already addresses it. The test at lines 199-203 explicitly removes `stability_tracker` from a serialized TankState to construct a genuine pre-v3 payload — this is exactly the pattern the amendment requests. Additionally, the documented migration contract (save.rs:47-48) requires adding a per-bump test, and all newly added TankState fields already use `#[serde(default)]`. The proposed generic regression test (removing an arbitrary field) is fragile, couples to current schema internals, and would need constant updating. The combination of the existing field-removal test demonstrating the correct pattern plus the mandatory per-bump test obligation provides adequate coverage. The remaining risk — that a future developer follows the weaker test pattern instead of the field-removal pattern — is a process concern better addressed by code review than by a perpetually-maintained regression test.

payload.summary: Rejected the single disputed amendment (fr-1-540a2c8b). While the amendment correctly identifies that 2 of 3 migration tests serialize current TankState with all current fields and merely relabel the schema version, the existing test at lines 199-203 already demonstrates the correct pattern by explicitly removing `stability_tracker` to simulate a true pre-v3 payload. Combined with the documented migration contract requiring per-bump tests and the consistent use of `#[serde(default)]` on all new fields, the current test infrastructure is adequate. The proposed generic regression test would be fragile and redundant with the per-bump obligation.
